title: Weak-field Nulloth backreaction
question: Does an active Nulloth coherence seed produce a controlled weak-field geometric response relative to an independently constraint-solved scalar-free control, and does that response scale with gravitational coupling?
prediction: Both the constraint-solved initial geometry and its subsequent evolution differ between active and scalar-free states. Doubling gravitational coupling produces an approximately doubled metric response while all constraints, conservation accounts, convexity margins, and recovery remain admissible.
falsifier: A vanishing dynamical geometric contrast, response scaling outside the declared weak-field window, failed conservation or entropy account, constraint violation, nonpositive convexity margin, or recovery failure falsifies the observation.
controls: Each active and scalar-free state receives an independent periodic CMC constraint solve.
The active and control pairs share gauge, matter, carrier modulation, grid, time step, and evolution duration.
The gravitational coupling is doubled from 5e-4 to 1e-3 to test weak-field scaling.
Initial constraint backreaction and subsequent dynamical response are reported separately.
No one-dimensional contrast is interpreted as transverse-traceless gravitational radiation.
seed_rationale: All initial profiles, constraint solves, and production evolutions are deterministic.
